cataract.title: Cataract
cataract.summary: Clouding of the eye's natural lens that makes vision blurry.
cataract.about: A cataract is a clouding of the normally clear lens of the eye. It usually develops slowly with age, but it can also be caused by diabetes, eye injury, long-term steroid use or too much sunlight. Cataract is one of the leading causes of reversible blindness in the world, and it is treated very successfully with surgery.
prevention: Wear sunglasses that block UV rays when outdoors
Do not smoke, and limit alcohol
Keep diabetes and blood pressure under control
Eat plenty of fruits and green leafy vegetables
Have regular eye checkups, especially after age 40
treatment: Early stage: stronger glasses, brighter lighting and anti-glare sunglasses
Cataract surgery: the cloudy lens is removed and replaced with a clear artificial lens (IOL)
Surgery is safe, quick and usually done as a day procedure
Follow the eye doctor's advice and use prescribed eye drops after surgery
cataract.see_doctor: See an eye specialist if your vision is getting blurry, glare makes driving or reading hard, or daily activities become difficult. Go urgently if you have sudden vision loss, eye pain or a red eye.

diabetic_retinopathy.title: Diabetic Retinopathy
diabetic_retinopathy.summary: Damage to the retina's blood vessels caused by diabetes.
diabetic_retinopathy.about: Diabetic retinopathy is an eye disease caused by high blood sugar damaging the small blood vessels of the retina, the light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye. In early stages there may be no symptoms. Over time vessels can leak, swell or grow abnormally, which can lead to serious vision loss if it is not treated. Everyone with diabetes is at risk.
symptoms: Often no symptoms in the early stages
Dark spots or floaters in vision
Dark or empty areas in the field of vision
prevention: Keep blood sugar (HbA1c) within the target set by your doctor
Control blood pressure and cholesterol
Have a dilated eye exam at least once a year if you have diabetes
Do not smoke
Exercise regularly and follow a healthy diet
Take diabetes medicines exactly as prescribed
treatment: Good control of blood sugar, blood pressure and cholesterol
Anti-VEGF injections into the eye to reduce swelling and abnormal vessels
Laser treatment (photocoagulation) to seal leaking vessels
Vitrectomy surgery for advanced cases with bleeding or scar tissue
Regular follow-up with an eye specialist
diabetic_retinopathy.see_doctor: If you have diabetes, see an eye specialist for a full retina exam every year even without symptoms. Go urgently if you notice sudden floaters, flashes of light, a dark curtain or sudden loss of vision.

glaucoma.title: Glaucoma
glaucoma.summary: Damage to the optic nerve, often linked to high eye pressure.
glaucoma.about: Glaucoma is a group of eye diseases that damage the optic nerve, which carries images from the eye to the brain. It is often related to high pressure inside the eye. The most common type develops slowly and without pain, so many people do not notice it until side vision is already lost. Vision lost from glaucoma cannot be recovered, but early treatment can stop or slow further damage.
symptoms: Often no symptoms in the early stages
Acute type: severe eye pain, headache, red eye
Acute type: blurred vision, halos around lights, nausea or vomiting
prevention: Have regular comprehensive eye exams, especially after age 40
Get checked more often if glaucoma runs in your family
Use prescribed eye drops regularly, even when you feel fine
Protect your eyes from injury (use protective eyewear)
Exercise regularly and keep a healthy lifestyle
treatment: Prescription eye drops to lower eye pressure
Laser treatment to improve fluid drainage
Surgery (e.g. trabeculectomy or drainage devices) when needed
Lifelong follow-up with an eye specialist
glaucoma.see_doctor: See an eye specialist soon for an eye pressure and optic nerve check. Go to the emergency department immediately if you have sudden severe eye pain, headache, red eye, blurred vision or nausea.

normal.title: Normal (Healthy Eye)
normal.summary: No signs of the screened diseases were found by the model.
normal.about: The model did not find signs of cataract, diabetic retinopathy or glaucoma in this image. This is good news, but it is not a guarantee of a healthy eye. Some eye conditions can only be found during a full examination by an eye specialist, so keep having regular checkups.
symptoms: No disease signs detected by the model
Still watch for blurry vision, eye pain, redness, flashes or floaters
prevention: Have a complete eye checkup every 1–2 years (every year if you have diabetes or are over 40)
Wear UV-blocking sunglasses outdoors
Follow the 20-20-20 rule for screens: every 20 minutes, look 20 feet away for 20 seconds
Eat a balanced diet with green leafy vegetables, fruits and fish
Do not smoke; control blood sugar and blood pressure
Wear protective eyewear during sports or risky work
treatment: No treatment needed based on this screening
Keep up regular eye checkups and healthy habits
normal.see_doctor: Visit an eye specialist for routine checkups, or sooner if you notice any change in vision, eye pain, redness, flashes of light or new floaters.
